question: How many cups of tea do people in the United Kingdom drink per day?

target.what: Total number of cups of tea consumed by people in the United Kingdom per day, averaged over a recent representative day (working interpretation: all tea beverages, hot and iced, consumed by UK residents and visitors within the UK, including tea made at home and out-of-home; excludes herbal/fruit inf
target.publisher: No single official publisher; UK Tea & Infusions Association (UKTIA) and ONS family food/retail data are the closest reference sources
target.cadence: Irregular / annual survey and trade-association statements
target.caveats: Ambiguity between cups consumed vs cups made; hot tea vs all tea; domestic consumption vs UK-wide including hospitality; per-person average day vs total annual divided by 365. candidates.data_to_find: UKTIA statements of average cups of tea drunk per person per day in the UK and any stated total daily cups; date of statement; definition (hot tea only vs all tea). Substitute: news articles quoting UKTIA figures.

assessment.note: All three trace to the same UKTIA/International Tea Committee headline of ~100 million cups/day (36 billion cups/year ÷ 365 ≈ 98.6 million). They are not independent measurements; they are one trade-association estimate repeated across outlets. Useful as an anchor but must be treated as a single source with unknown vintage and method.

Statista's 72 million kg/year (p135) and the 3 g/cup conversion (p40) plus tea-bag weights of 2–3.1 g (p59–p61) are mutually consistent: 72e6 kg × ~333 cups/kg ≈ 24 billion cups/year ≈ 66 million cups/day. WITS bilateral black-tea import records (2023 HS 090240 and 2024 HS 090230) are the same underlying customs measurement from different reporters/years. They give a partial black-tea import floor (~90–110 million kg across lines) but omit green/other tea, stock change, and re-exports, so they support a supply-based lower bound rather than a full total.

methods.label: m1

p135.role: UK annual tea consumption in kg (Statista, excludes herbal/RTD/instant), recent year

a2.role: cups per kg of dry tea

methods.rationale: Supply/volume route: Statista's 72 million kg/year UK tea consumption converted to cups via ~333 cups/kg and divided by 365. Independent of the UKTIA headline; likely a lower bound because it excludes herbal/RTD/instant and out-of-home, but the target excludes herbal/fruit, so scope is close. Shared dependency: a2 conversion factor; failure mode if Statista volume is stale or excludes hospitality.

methods.label: m2

p34.role: UKTIA stated UK cups of tea per day

methods.rationale: Direct trade-association headline of >100 million cups/day, corroborated by p128/p129 (36 billion cups/year). Single underlying source (UKTIA/ITC) with unknown vintage; treated as one anchor, not independent confirmation. Failure mode: figure may be dated (pre-decline) and generous.

methods.label: m3

p87.role: UK total world imports of black tea (HS 090230), 2024, kg

a2.role: cups per kg of dry tea

methods.rationale: Physical-flow floor from 2024 UK black-tea imports (11.18 million kg) converted to cups. Covers only black tea imports, omitting green/other tea, stock change, and re-exports, so declared as a part and not combined with full estimates. Shared dependency: a2; failure mode if HS 090230 undercounts total tea.

methods.label: m4

a5.role: share of population who are adults

a3.role: share of UK adults drinking tea on a given day

a4.role: mean cups per tea drinker per day

methods.rationale: Capacity x frequency decomposition: population x adult share x daily-drinking prevalence x mean cups per drinker. Prevalence and frequency anchored to YouGov generational shares (p116-p122, p112) and the distributional survey (p105-p107). Independent of supply and headline routes. Failure modes: prevalence uncertainty is the dominant term; survey framing differences (p104/p127 vs YouGov) are large
methods.error: formula_mc must use at least one kept observed data point (a formula made only of assumptions is rejected)

kept.name: Cups per kg of dry tea (inverse of grams per cup)
kept.rationale: Derived from 2-3.1 g per bag (p59-p61) and the 3 g/cup convention (p40); 333 cups/kg corresponds to 3 g/cup, with range spanning 2-4 g/cup.
kept.applies_when: Converting UK tea mass (kg) to cups for a recent year.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that typical UK cups use materially more or less than 2-4 g of dry tea.

kept.name: Share of UK adults drinking tea on a given day
kept.rationale: YouGov generational daily shares (p116-p122, 11-32%) and the 41% 'twice a day' figure (p112) imply a moderate daily prevalence; the 90-98% claims (p104, p127) are implausibly high. Assumed central 45% with wide range.
kept.applies_when: Capacity x frequency decomposition of daily cups for UK adults.
kept.falsified_by: A representative survey showing daily tea-drinking prevalence well outside 30-60%.

kept.name: Mean cups per tea drinker per day
kept.rationale: Distributional survey (p105-p107: 44% one-two, 35% three-four, 20% five-six) implies a mean around 2.5-3 cups among drinkers; assumed 2.5 with wide range.
kept.applies_when: Capacity x frequency decomposition of daily cups for UK adults.
kept.falsified_by: A representative survey showing mean cups per drinker outside 1.5-4.

kept.name: Share of UK population who are adults
kept.rationale: ONS: adults (~18+) are roughly 78% of the UK population; used to apply adult-based prevalence to the national total.
kept.applies_when: Scaling adult survey prevalence to the whole UK population.
kept.falsified_by: ONS age structure showing adult share outside 75-81%.

kept.name: UK resident population 2025
kept.rationale: ONS mid-year UK population is ~68-69 million in the mid-2020s; used to convert per-capita prevalence into a national daily total. No kept point supplies population, so it is assumed.
kept.applies_when: Converting adult prevalence and frequency into a national daily cup total for 2025.
kept.falsified_by: An ONS 2025 population estimate outside 68-70 million.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
